questions.question: Which of the following best describes the range of subjects Rembrandt depicted in his works?
options: Portraits, self-portraits, landscapes, genre scenes, allegorical and historical scenes, biblical and mythological subjects, and animal studies
Only portraits and self-portraits
Only landscapes and genre scenes
Only biblical and mythological subjects
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Rembrandt's works depict a wide range of styles and subject matter, listing portraits, self-portraits, landscapes, genre scenes, allegorical and historical scenes, biblical and mythological subjects, and animal studies.
Incorrect. The article explicitly mentions that Rembrandt's works include many subjects beyond just portraits and self-portraits.
Incorrect. The article notes that Rembrandt also painted portraits, self-portraits, and other subjects, not just landscapes and genre scenes.
Incorrect. The article lists many other subjects besides biblical and mythological ones.

questions.question: What was the name of the person Rembrandt married in 1634?
options: Saskia van Uylenburgh
Hendrickje Stoffels
Geertje Dircx
Neeltgen Willemsdochter van Zuijtbrouck
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says Rembrandt married Hendrick's cousin, Saskia van Uylenburgh, in 1634.
Incorrect. Hendrickje Stoffels was his later companion, not his wife.
Incorrect. Geertje Dircx was a caretaker and later lover, not his wife.
Incorrect. Neeltgen Willemsdochter van Zuijtbrouck was his mother.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Rembrandt's financial situation is supported by the article?
options: He declared insolvency in July 1656 and surrendered his assets.
He never faced any financial difficulties.
He became wealthy and never sold his possessions.
He was forced into bankruptcy by his creditors.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article notes that in July 1656, Rembrandt declared his insolvency, took stock, and willingly surrendered his assets.
Incorrect. The article details his financial turmoil, insolvency, and asset sales.
Incorrect. The article describes his financial difficulties and the sale of his possessions.
Incorrect. The article states his bankruptcy was not forced; he voluntarily declared insolvency.

questions.question: What was the name of the street where Rembrandt's house was located in 1639?
options: Breestraat
Jodenbreestraat
Rozengracht
Vlooienburg
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says in May 1639 they moved to a recently modernised house in the upscale 'Breestraat' (Jodenbreestraat).
Incorrect. While Breestraat is mentioned, the article clarifies it is also known as Jodenbreestraat, but the specific street name given is Breestraat.
Incorrect. Rozengracht is where they moved later, not in 1639.
Incorrect. Vlooienburg is a location he moved to in 1637, not the street in 1639.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between Rembrandt and Hendrickje Stoffels?
options: She was initially his maid and later his companion, with whom he had a daughter.
She was his wife.
She was his student.
She was his patron.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says Hendrickje Stoffels was initially his maid, later his companion, and they had a daughter, Cornelia.
Incorrect. Hendrickje Stoffels was not his wife; his wife was Saskia van Uylenburgh.
Incorrect. Hendrickje Stoffels was not listed as a student; she was his maid and companion.
Incorrect. Hendrickje Stoffels was not his patron; she was his companion.

questions.question: Which of the following was a significant event in Rembrandt's later years involving his son Titus?
options: Titus drafted a will in 1655 designating his father as the sole heir.
Titus died in 1641.
Titus became a famous painter.
Titus moved to the Dutch East Indies.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article mentions that in November 1655, Rembrandt's 14-year-old son Titus drafted a will designating his father as the sole heir.
Incorrect. Titus was born in 1641 and survived into adulthood; he did not die then.
Incorrect. The article does not state that Titus became a famous painter.
Incorrect. Titus remained in the Netherlands; his illegitimate child moved to Batavia.

questions.question: What was the outcome of the church council regarding Hendrickje Stoffels?
options: She was banned from receiving communion.
She was excommunicated from the church.
She was acquitted of the charges.
She was appointed as a church official.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says Hendrickje admitted her guilt and was banned from receiving communion.
Incorrect. The article only mentions she was banned from communion, not excommunicated.
Incorrect. She admitted guilt and was punished, not acquitted.
Incorrect. There is no mention of her being appointed as a church official.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the nature of Rembrandt's self-portraits?
options: They form an intimate autobiography, with approximately 100 self-portraits, over 40 of which are paintings.
They were all painted in his early career.
They were all done in oil on canvas.
They were all done in a single year.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Rembrandt's approximately 100 self-portraits, over 40 of which are paintings, form an intimate autobiography.
Incorrect. The self-portraits span his career, not just early years.
Incorrect. While many are oil paintings, the article does not claim all were oil on canvas.
Incorrect. The self-portraits were created over many years, not in a single year.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the fate of Rembrandt's painting 'The Conspiracy of Claudius Civilis'?
options: It was rejected by the mayors and only a fragment survives.
It was widely praised and is now in a major museum.
It was never completed.
It was sold to a private collector.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says the work was rejected by the mayors and returned to the painter; the surviving fragment is only a quarter of the original.
Incorrect. The article notes it was rejected, not praised.
Incorrect. The article says the work was completed but rejected.
Incorrect. The article does not mention a sale; it was rejected and returned.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the content of Rembrandt's letter to Huygens about his artistic goals?
options: He sought to achieve 'the greatest and most natural movement' (de meeste en de natuurlijkste beweegelijkheid).
He wanted to paint only portraits.
He wanted to paint only landscapes.
He wanted to paint only biblical scenes.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article quotes Rembrandt's letter to Huygens, stating he sought 'the greatest and most natural movement' (de meeste en de natuurlijkste beweegelijkheid).
Incorrect. The article does not say he wanted to paint only portraits; it mentions his broader range of subjects.
Incorrect. The article does not say he wanted to paint only landscapes.
Incorrect. The article does not say he wanted to paint only biblical scenes.
